review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὸ Ἀρνίον μίαν ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ σφραγίδων, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγοντος ὡς φωνῇ βροντῆς Ἔρχου.
6:1.targetText: Then I watched as the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures say in a thunderous voice, “Come!”

groups.note: ὡς … βροντῆς ("as of thunder") is rendered by the adjective thunderous.
The dative φωνῇ ("with a voice") is rendered in a … voice.

6:2.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων τόξον, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στέφανος, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν νικῶν καὶ ἵνα νικήσῃ.
6:2.targetText: So I looked and saw a white horse, and its rider held a bow. And he was given a crown, and he rode out to overcome and conquer.

groups.note: ἰδού ("look!") is rendered saw after I looked.
ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτόν ("the one seated on it") is rendered its rider.
The participle ἔχων ("having") is rendered as a finite verb.
The participle νικῶν ("conquering") is drawn into BSB's purpose phrase.
ἵνα ("in order that") gives the purpose; BSB's one to covers both verbs.

6:3.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν δευτέραν, ἤκουσα τοῦ δευτέρου ζῴου λέγοντος Ἔρχου.
6:3.targetText: And when the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come!”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject from 6:1; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

6:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἄλλος ἵππος πυρρός, καὶ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἐδόθη αὐτῷ λαβεῖν τὴν εἰρήνην ἐκ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἵνα ἀλλήλους σφάξουσιν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ μάχαιρα μεγάλη.
6:4.targetText: Then another horse went forth. It was bright red, and its rider was granted permission to take away peace from the earth and to make men slay one another. And he was given a great sword.

groups.note: τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτόν ("to the one seated on it") is rendered its rider.
ἵνα ("in order that") is rendered to.

unmappedSource.reason: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") repeats τῷ καθημένῳ and has no separate English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English starts a new sentence with a subject and copula; the Greek has only the adjective πυρρός.
English names what was granted; the Greek says only that it was given him to take peace.
English adds a causative verb; the Greek says that they would slay one another.
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of σφάξουσιν.

6:5.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τρίτην, ἤκουσα τοῦ τρίτου ζῴου λέγοντος Ἔρχου. καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος μέλας, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων ζυγὸν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
6:5.targetText: And when the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come!”  Then I looked and saw a black horse, and its rider held in his hand a pair of scales.

groups.note: ἰδού ("look!") is rendered saw after I looked.
ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτόν ("the one seated on it") is rendered its rider.
The participle ἔχων ("having") is rendered as a finite verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject from 6:1; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

6:6.sourceText: καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγουσαν Χοῖνιξ σίτου δηναρίου, καὶ τρεῖς χοίνικες κριθῶν δηναρίου· καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον καὶ τὸν οἶνον μὴ ἀδικήσῃς.
6:6.targetText: And I heard what sounded like a voice from among the four living creatures, saying, “A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius, and do not harm the oil and wine.”

groups.note: ἐν μέσῳ ("in the midst of") is rendered from among, the place the voice came from.
The genitive of price δηναρίου is rendered for a denarius.
The genitive of price δηναρίου is rendered for a denarius.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB uses one the for oil and wine, so this article has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English expands the comparison; the Greek has only ὡς ("like") before a voice.

6:7.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τετάρτην, ἤκουσα φωνὴν τοῦ τετάρτου ζῴου λέγοντος Ἔρχου.
6:7.targetText: And when the Lamb opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, “Come!”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject from 6:1; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

6:8.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος χλωρός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ὁ Θάνατος, καὶ ὁ Ἅιδης ἠκολούθει μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἐξουσία ἐπὶ τὸ τέταρτον τῆς γῆς, ἀποκτεῖναι ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ καὶ ἐν λιμῷ καὶ ἐν θανάτῳ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῆς γῆς.
6:8.targetText: Then I looked and saw a pale green horse. Its rider’s name was Death, and Hades followed close behind. And they were given authority over a fourth of the earth, to kill by sword, by famine, by plague, and by the beasts of the earth.

groups.note: ἰδού ("look!") is rendered saw after I looked.
ὁ καθήμενος ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ("the one seated on it") is rendered Its rider, and the dative αὐτῷ ("to him") gives the possessive ’s.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
μετ’ αὐτοῦ ("with him") is rendered close behind.
θάνατος ("death") here means deadly disease, rendered plague.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB lists the means with commas, so καί has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.

6:9.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν πέμπτην σφραγῖδα, εἶδον ὑποκάτω τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐσφαγμένων διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν εἶχον.
6:9.targetText: And when the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for the testimony they had upheld.

targetPhrases.text: of those who had been slain

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ἥν ("which") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject from 6:1; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

6:10.sourceText: καὶ ἔκραξαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες Ἕως πότε, ὁ Δεσπότης ὁ ἅγιος καὶ ἀληθινός, οὐ κρίνεις καὶ ἐκδικεῖς τὸ αἷμα ἡμῶν ἐκ τῶν κατοικούντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
6:10.targetText: And they cried out in a loud voice, “How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You avenge our blood and judge those who dwell upon the earth?”

groups.note: With Ἕως ("until"), πότε ("when?") forms the question How long … until.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB introduces the quotation without a word for λέγοντες ("saying").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts "how long will You not judge" as "how long until You avenge … and judge", so οὐ has no English word.
BSB makes those who dwell the object of judge, so ἐκ ("from") has no English word.

6:11.sourceText: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἑκάστῳ στολὴ λευκή, καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα ἀναπαύσωνται ἔτι χρόνον μικρόν, ἕως πληρωθῶσιν καὶ οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν οἱ μέλλοντες ἀποκτέννεσθαι ὡς καὶ αὐτοί.
6:11.targetText: Then each of them was given a white robe and told to rest a little while longer, until the full number of their fellow servants, their brothers, were killed, just as they had been killed.

groups.note: BSB's Greek has another form of this verb here; the meaning is the same.
πληρωθῶσιν ("are made complete") is rendered the full number of.
ἀποκτέννεσθαι ("to be killed") is rendered were killed, and BSB repeats it in been killed, the verb that ὡς καὶ αὐτοί leaves understood.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB keeps each of them as the subject of told, so the second αὐτοῖς has no English word.
BSB leaves this καί ("also") untranslated.
BSB sets their brothers beside their fellow servants with a comma, so καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB makes the infinitive the main verb were killed and has no word for οἱ μέλλοντες ("who are about to").
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a past-perfect tense to the repeated verb; the Greek clause has no verb.

6:12.sourceText: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἕκτην, καὶ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ ἥλιος ἐγένετο μέλας ὡς σάκκος τρίχινος, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὅλη ἐγένετο ὡς αἷμα,
6:12.targetText: And when I saw the Lamb open the sixth seal, there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black like sackcloth of goat hair, and the whole moon turned blood red,

groups.note: ὡς αἷμα ("like blood") is rendered blood red.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins this clause to the when clause with a comma, so καί has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.
English specifies the hair; τρίχινος means only "made of hair".

6:13.sourceText: καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔπεσαν εἰς τὴν γῆν, ὡς συκῆ βάλλει τοὺς ὀλύνθους αὐτῆς ὑπὸ ἀνέμου μεγάλου σειομένη,
6:13.targetText: and the stars of the sky fell to the earth like unripe figs dropping from a tree shaken by a great wind.

groups.note: συκῆ ("fig tree") is rendered tree.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts the clause around the figs, so αὐτῆς ("its") has no English word.

6:14.sourceText: καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ἀπεχωρίσθη ὡς βιβλίον ἑλισσόμενον, καὶ πᾶν ὄρος καὶ νῆσος ἐκ τῶν τόπων αὐτῶν ἐκινήθησαν.
6:14.targetText: The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved from its place.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:15.sourceText: καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ μεγιστᾶνες καὶ οἱ χιλίαρχοι καὶ οἱ πλούσιοι καὶ οἱ ἰσχυροὶ καὶ πᾶς δοῦλος καὶ ἐλεύθερος ἔκρυψαν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς τὰ σπήλαια καὶ εἰς τὰς πέτρας τῶν ὀρέων,
6:15.targetText: Then the kings of the earth, the nobles, the commanders, the rich, the mighty, and every slave and free man hid in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains.

groups.note: ἔκρυψαν ἑαυτούς ("hid themselves") is rendered hid.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists these groups with commas, so καί has no English word.

6:16.sourceText: καὶ λέγουσιν τοῖς ὄρεσιν καὶ ταῖς πέτραις Πέσετε ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς καὶ κρύψατε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς τοῦ Ἀρνίου,
6:16.targetText: And they said to the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of the One seated on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb.

6:17.sourceText: ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ἡμέρα ἡ μεγάλη τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτῶν, καὶ τίς δύναται σταθῆναι;
6:17.targetText: For the great day of Their wrath has come, and who is able to withstand it?”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for withstand; the Greek has only the infinitive.
